record.paper_title: Higher Rank Brill-Noether Theory and Coherent Systems: Open Questions
record.original_question: Let C be a smooth projective curve over the complex numbers. What is the dimension of each irreducible component of the Brill-Noether locus B(n,d,k)?

evidence.quote: Question 2.4. What is the dimension (of each component) of B(n, d, k)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $C$ be a smooth projective irreducible curve of genus $g \ge 2$ over the complex numbers. For integers $n \ge 1$, $d$, and $k \ge 1$, let $M(n,d)$ denote the moduli space of (semi)stable vector bundles on $C$ of rank $n$ and degree $d$, and define the higher-rank Brill–Noether locus
$$B(n,d,k) \;=\; \{\, [E] \in M(n,d) \,:\, h^0(C,E) \ge k \,\}.$$
The expected (Brill–Noether) dimension of $B(n,d,k)$ is
$$\beta(n,d,k) \;=\; n^2(g-1) + 1 - k\bigl(k - d + n(g-1)\bigr).$$
Determine the dimension of each irreducible component of $B(n,d,k)$. Equivalently: for which triples $(n,d,k)$ does every irreducible component of $B(n,d,k)$ have dimension equal to $\beta(n,d,k)$, and in the remaining cases describe the possible dimensions of the components.
artifact.status_search_result: The dimension of each irreducible component of the higher-rank Brill–Noether locus B(n,d,k) is known only in special cases. On a general curve, B(n,d,k) can be empty when β>0 and nonempty when β<0, and it can be reducible with components of different dimensions. Lower bounds (e.g., dim ≥ β when k > d − n(g−1)) and the existence of components of the expected dimension have been established under various hypotheses (Teixidor i Bigas, Mercat, and others), and recent work continues to determine components in further regimes, but a complete answer remains unavailable.

status_evidence.title: Universal extension spaces and modular maps: irreducible components of Brill-Noether loci
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work identifies new irreducible components of B(n,d,k) on general ν-gonal curves.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results on components and their dimensions continue to appear.

status_evidence.title: Martens and Mumford theorems for higher rank Brill–Noether loci
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes dimension bounds analogous to classical Martens/Mumford theorems for B(n,d,k).
status_evidence.claim: Only bounds (not exact dimensions) are known in general.
